label: <DEL> step after an original sequence rich in h/i/p/g/u/o/j/digits
explanation: Almost all of its activity is on the delimiter step: 93% of activation mass is at <DEL>, which fires on 11.6% of sequences (lift 11.6x). It is nearly silent in the original phase (5% of mass, mostly on w/s/e/z/k inputs at t=4..9) and in the copy phase (1.5%). Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on what the original sequence contained. It is pushed up by h, i, p, g, u, o, j and digits (more digits means a higher rate: 0.6x with 0 digits, 2.4x with 4), and h or i in the last one or two positions is the strongest cue. It is pushed down by w, s, e, z, k, y, b. The top activations are all short sequences made mostly of h/i/digits/p, e.g. p 3 i h h <DEL>. A count rule (positive-token count minus negative-token count >= 2 at <DEL>) captures 86% of the mass on dev, but precision is only about 0.27. The real readout looks like a graded, distributed weighting over the prefix tokens, and a simple set count does not reproduce it, so the explanation is only partial.
